finding.explanation: The committed claims use the same normalized subject and object but make opposed direct causal assertions (causes versus prevents).

observations.text: Of 1,321 entries in the learnings register, 638 describe themselves as a repeat of something already recorded, and zero have been promoted into a check that binds.

A lesson recorded at 21:58 was surfaced at the top of a later turn by the recall mechanism, and the agent receiving it committed that exact failure inside the same turn. The loop collects and delivers; it does not bind.

Recurring lessons are not more mechanisable than average: 35 percent of repeats name something runnable against 30 percent of non-repeats. Recurrence tells you what a failure costs, not whether it can be automated.
The promotion machinery that would turn a stable finding into a deterministic check exists, and its input has never been produced.
An installer defect that writes byte-identical duplicate scripts into every governed repository was recorded twice on 2026-08-21, and a new governed repository received it unchanged eight days later.

A feedback mechanism that watches work needs something watching it, and the regress is affordable only when each meta-level is the same mechanism applied to its own output rather than a new system built to supervise the old one.

proposal.answer: The supplied observations support a bounded proposal: lessons recur because collection and recall do not transform them into binding checks, while the available promotion machinery remains unfed. This is a stress-test proposal, not a factual certification.
